newsitem.title: USA: Denbury confirms four dead in rig mishap.
newsitem.headline: Denbury confirms four dead in rig mishap.

text.p: Two workers, missing following a blowout on a drilling rig in the swampy waters of southern Louisiana, have been found dead, Denbury Resources Inc said Wednesday.
Two other workers were confirmed killed late Monday when a high pressure stream of gas burst from the well, igniting and shooting a 200-foot column of flames into the sky.
"There are now four that are confirmed fatalities," said Phil Rykhoek, chief financial officer for Dallas-based Denbury. Eighteen other crewmen were evacuated earlier from the burning rig.
The rig was completing a well on the Lake Chicot gas field, about 40 miles southwest of Baton Rouge in Louisiana's bayou country. Denbury is the field's operator.
Rykhoek said the well was still blowing an estimated 20 million cubic feet a day (mmcfd) of gas.

"It was a new well in the process of completion. We've engaged International Well Control to get it under control. They're hoping to commence well control in the next day or two, as soon as all the necessary equipment arrives," he said.
The Lake Chicot gas field is currently producing about one mmcfd from seven wells.
Rykhoek said this latest well would have been the best on the field, with a projected flow rate of about five mmcfd.
"We anticipate we can salvage the well, but the rig is pretty much a total loss," he said.
Mallard Bay Drilling, a subsidiary of Parker Drilling Co was carrying out the well completion work using a barge-mounted drilling rig.
